module_description: Examines aviation forecast products and specific high-impact hazards on a global scale. Covers the structure and effective writing of TAFs, tracking and impacts of Tropical Storms and Volcanic Ash, and decoding global WAFC SIGWX charts.
competencies: Produce clear, concise, and accurate Terminal Aerodrome Forecasts (TAFs) tailored to operational needs
Apply appropriate change groups and amendment criteria to TAFs
Interpret advisories and track forecasts for tropical cyclones and volcanic ash
Decode global high-level and medium-level SIGWX charts from World Area Forecast Centres

learning_objectives: Define TAF structure and terminology, including the operational definition of Vicinity (VC)
Apply TAF writing philosophy to generate concise and user-friendly forecasts
Categorize weather conditions into standard aviation flight categories (VFR, IFR)
visual_elements_needed: Worked TAF example with color-coded groups illustrating the structure

learning_objectives: Formulate appropriate change groups (BECMG, TEMPO) for deteriorating or improving conditions
Evaluate existing TAFs for ambiguity and propose operational amendments
Discriminate between scenarios requiring TEMPO versus PROB groups
visual_elements_needed: Flowchart for deciding between change groups (BECMG, TEMPO, PROB)

learning_objectives: Describe the atmospheric conditions required for tropical storm formation
Classify tropical cyclones using the Saffir-Simpson scale
Interpret global warning center advisories and graphical track forecasts
visual_elements_needed: Track-forecast diagram (cone of uncertainty) showing the cyclone's predicted path
external_imagery_needed: Satellite image of a tropical storm (e.g., a Mediterranean storm relevant to IMS forecasting)

learning_objectives: Explain the specific hazards volcanic ash poses to jet aircraft operations
Interpret Volcanic Ash Advisories (VAA) from VAACs
Outline the role of atmospheric dispersion modeling for predicting ash plume trajectories
visual_elements_needed: SIGMET dispersion-area sketch illustrating an ash plume polygon
external_imagery_needed: Photograph of a volcanic ash plume from a real eruption

learning_objectives: Distinguish between High-level (SWH) and Medium-level (SWM) SIGWX charts
Decode standard aviation meteorological parameters (jetstreams, CAT, CBs) on WAFC maps
Differentiate between isolated, occasional, and frequent cumulonimbus coverage as defined by ICAO
visual_elements_needed: Annotated mock-WAFC-chart showing jetstreams, CAT areas, and tropopause heights

module_quiz.description: End-of-module summative assessment covering TAFs, global hazards, and WAFC charts
